identity.title: An Analysis of ALMA Deep Fields and the Perceived Dearth of High-z Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: we extend the backward evolution galaxy model described by Casey et. al. (2018) to the ALMA regime (in depth and area)

targets.name: ASPECS-Pilot, HUDF, GOODS-ALMA, SSA22, SXDF ALMA deep fields (literature)

question.value: Are the low numbers of high-z dusty galaxies in ALMA deep fields consistent with a backward-evolution IRLF model constrained by single-dish surveys, and how should future ALMA surveys be designed?

evidence.quote: the measured number counts and redshift distributions from ALMA deep field surveys are fully consistent with constraints of the infrared luminosity function (IRLF) at $z<2.5$

evidence.quote: We have built a backward-evolution model to interpret the origins of emission in the submillimeter/millimeter sky from galaxy number counts, redshift distributions and correlations between bands.

method.value: Inject IRLF-derived sources with SEDs into mock maps, convolve with beam, add noise, re-extract sources

evidence.quote: Once all sources at all redshifts have been injected into these mock maps, they are convolved with the beamsize of observations specific to a certain instrument at a certain observatory

key_parameters.value: Pixel size 1/5 of minimum beam FWHM; Band 6 beam 0.6" and RMS 13 uJy

evidence.quote: A mock map consists of a regularly-spaced grid with pixel size equal to 1/5 of the minimum beamsize FWHM simulated

analysis_steps.goal: Fit faint-end slope to HUDF source density

method.value: Vary alpha_LF in -1 to -0.1 for Models A and B; count >3.5 sigma sources at 35 uJy RMS; 100 Monte Carlo runs per value

evidence.loc: 3.1 Importance of the Faint-End Slope of the IRLF
evidence.quote: we constrain the number of expected sources and its uncertainty by using 100 Monte Carlo simulations for either Model A or Model B.

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate completeness and contamination and compare number counts and redshift distributions

method.value: Run detection on inverted maps and compare injected vs detected catalogues; compare with literature counts and redshift distributions using random subsets of n=5 or 15

evidence.quote: we invert the maps and run our source detection algorithm on the negative image, where we know all detections will be false.

method.value: Generate SED family with mid-IR power law, find SEDs matching observed 1.2 mm flux, derive LIR probability density, combine with LUV to get IRX

evidence.quote: We then search for all possible SEDs that have the observed flux density at 1.2 mm and use it to generate a probability density distribution in $L_{\rm IR}$.

findings_qualitative.value: 1.2 mm deep fields are unconstraining for the high-z IRLF; 2 mm wider, shallower surveys are optimal

evidence.quote: We find 1.2 mm ALMA deep fields completely unconstraining for the high-redshift IRLF.

claims.hypothesis: ALMA deep-field counts and redshifts are consistent with single-dish-constrained IRLF
claims.experiment: Mock ALMA maps from the extended C18 model compared with literature counts
claims.result: Good agreement in counts; redshift data cannot distinguish models
claims.finding: No dearth of high-z dusty galaxies is implied

evidence.quote: A simple extension of the C18 models appears to reproduce the 1.2 mm ALMA number counts well

claims.experiment: Re-derived IRX with different SEDs and IRX-beta reference

evidence.quote: conclude that there is no evidence for less dust in high-$z$ UV-selected galaxy populations

claims.hypothesis: A 2 mm ALMA survey can discriminate models
claims.result: 20 (Model A) to 120 detections over ~230 arcmin^2 at 0.08 mJy RMS

evidence.quote: would result in 20 (Model A) to 120 detections (Models B & C)

limitations_admitted.value: Sources are modelled as point sources, and observed samples are small

evidence.quote: The comparison is a bit unfair, given that we are limited to a handful of galaxies in each sample

Contamination estimates depend on the assumed detection algorithm
